# Which group an entry lands in, and why

A top-level entry's group comes from the string it FILES under — its sort key
where it has one, its printed text where it does not. Every entry below is
written so that one of those two paths reaches one of the two outcomes, a
letter group or the leading Symbols group.

Printed text, reaching a letter: [zebra]{.index}.

Printed text, reaching Symbols, and the first of the pair whose adjacency is
the point: [\#hashtag]{.index}.

The second of that pair. Between `#` and `~` in character order sit every
letter and every digit, so these two are neighbours only because the letters
have been lifted out into groups of their own — an index that merely sorted by
character code would print half the alphabet between them:
[\~tilde]{.index}.

A sort key, reaching a letter: the entry prints as a symbol but files under a
word, so it leaves Symbols altogether:
[\#1 priority]{.index sort="alpha priority"}.

A sort key, reaching Symbols: the entry prints as a word but files under a
symbol, so it leaves its letter group. The key is written `!!` because a
single `!` separates sort levels — this key is one level whose first character
is a literal exclamation mark: [Quixote]{.index sort="!!quixote"}.

An entry whose printed text begins outside ASCII files under Symbols, which is
honest about a collation that only folds ASCII: [éclair]{.index}.

An entry with no top-level text at all — an empty filing string, which is not
a letter either: [sub]{.index entry="!windmill"}.

Two more letters, so the alphabet's own order is visible: [alpha]{.index} and
[Mango]{.index}.
